en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Fifth Chapter
The Discourse on the Path of Certainty: Is there knowledge for one who is not yet certain to go toward the path of certainty?
Yes, there is.
Is there knowledge for one who is destined [for the fixed course] to go upon the undetermined course?
One should not say so…pe… Is there no knowledge for one who is destined [for the fixed course] to go upon the undetermined course?
“Yes.
“Then there is no knowledge for the sake of entering the fixed course for one who is not yet fixed?
You should not say so… [and so on].
Is there knowledge for one who is undetermined to go to the fixed course? Yes.
Is there knowledge for one who is determined to go to the fixed course?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there no knowledge for the sake of one who is destined to go to the fixed course? Yes.
Is there no knowledge for one who is undetermined to go to the fixed course?
One should not say so… [as before] … Is there knowledge for one who is undetermined to go to the fixed course?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is there knowledge for one who is undetermined regarding the going upon the undetermined path?
You must not say so … [and so on].
Is it the case that for one who is undetermined, there is no knowledge of going into the undetermined state?
Yes. Is it the case that for one who is undetermined, there is no knowledge of going into the determined state?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is there knowledge for the sake of entering the fixed course of one who is undetermined? Yes.
Is there a "fixed course" for the sake of one who is unfixed proceeding toward the fixed course?
One should not say so... [and so on] ...
Is there knowledge for the sake of one who is unfixed proceeding toward the fixed course?
“Yes.
“For one who is undetermined, there are foundations of mindfulness for the sake of entering the fixed course of rightness… there are right efforts…”
The bases of psychic power … the faculties … the powers …
Are they called "factors of enlightenment"?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is there no fixed course for one who is undetermined in order to enter the fixed course? One should not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].
But if there is no fixed course for one who is unfixed in order to enter the fixed course, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
“There is knowledge for one who is unfixed in order to enter the fixed course.”
Is it not the case that for one who is undetermined, there are no foundations of mindfulness ... nor factors of enlightenment, for the sake of entering the path of determination?
Yes, it is.
If there are no factors of enlightenment for one who is not fixed in destiny to enter the fixed path, then indeed it should not be said:
"There is knowledge for one who is not fixed in destiny to enter the fixed path.
Is there knowledge for one who is not fixed in destiny to enter the fixed path?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does a person who is in the lineage (gotrabhū) possess knowledge of the path of stream-entry?
You should not say so …pe…
Is it to be said that a person who is practicing for the realization of the fruit of stream-entry possesses knowledge regarding the fruit of stream-entry?
Certainly not. …pe… Is it to be said that a person who is practicing for the realization of arhatship possesses knowledge regarding arhatship?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Should it not be said:
“There is knowledge for one who is undetermined to enter the fixed course”?
“Yes, [he does].
“But does not the Blessed One know:
‘This person will enter the fixed course of rightness; this person is capable of realizing the Dhamma’?”
“Yes.
“If the Blessed One knows:
‘This person will enter the fixed course of rightness; this person is capable of realizing the Dhamma,’ then indeed, sir, you should say:”
“There is knowledge for one who is not fixed in destiny to enter the fixed course.
The Discussion on the Fixed Course is finished.
